principles.rule: Find a repeatable viral format yourself before paying creators or scaling accounts.
principles.why: Hiring is 'probably 5% of it'; creators are hired to film, not to figure out how to go viral. Founders who know the format can brief and train creators.

principles.rule: Once a format hits, replicate it over and over; only vary the hook.
principles.why: Alberto gets 2-5M views/month and 100K downloads from essentially one slideshow format; roughly 1 in 6 posts goes viral in Spain.

principles.rule: Post 1-3 times per day per account, every day, and push through the zero-traction phase.
principles.why: Larry posts 3/day minimum; Alberto 3/day; Jack (Lovely) and Max Blade (Talk Macros) about 2/day, and days without posts showed fewer new subs. Buffer: accounts posting in 20+ of 26 weeks get ~450% more engagement per post than sporadic posters.
principles.source: Larry skill (clawhub.ai/olliewazza/skills/larry); Adam Lyttle https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HjnXnssrj4M; Buffer creator growth playbook

principles.rule: Spend most effort on slide 1 / the first 1-3 seconds; use specific person+conflict+reveal hooks.
principles.why: Larry's winners were 'I showed my mum/nan what AI thinks our living room could be' (170K-300K views); his analysis found the winners are curiosity 'reveals', not insults. Hook families: 'What AI thinks' reveal, time-shock ('hasn't changed since 1989'), forbidden/defiance ('my landlord said I can't change anything').
principles.source: Oliver Henry on Greg Isenberg podcast, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OV5eK91YY68 (transcript)

principles.rule: The CTA slide must name the app and the outcome; make it feel discovered, not advertised.
principles.why: 'She's redecorating now. Snugly' got ~300K views and almost no downloads; 'The Snugly app helped me finally convince her to get the kitchen done' converted. Alberto: 'find a way for the user to feel they found your app, not the reverse'.

principles.rule: Design one dramatic 'wow' screen (or widget) specifically to be shown on social.
principles.why: Dramatic screenshots make viewers ask for the app; widgets were the wow moment in Alberto's two best apps; Nicole spends day 2 in Figma designing 'the screen that will go viral'.

principles.rule: Prefer realistic, slightly imperfect visuals; avoid AI-looking images and AI humans.
principles.why: Early DALL-E 3 images and AI faces flopped ('humans are extremely good at recognizing an AI human'); an imperfect image with a missing oven became the best post (~400K) because commenters piled in to point out the mistake.

principles.rule: Optimize for installs and revenue, not views: connect RevenueCat/Stripe and diagnose with a views x conversion 2x2.
principles.why: High views + low conversion = fix CTA; low views + high conversion rate = fix hook; both low = reset; both high = scale; installs but no payers = fix onboarding/paywall. Views alone mislead (vendor example: 500K views -> ~40 installs).
principles.source: Larry skill; LarryLoop; TokPortal use case (vendor)

principles.rule: Winners decay: rotate between winning hooks and retire a hook when its hit rate drops.
principles.why: Oliver's best 'landlord' hook fell to 'one video in five' (132K -> 8K -> 7K -> 4K) and the agent stopped using it automatically.

principles.rule: Start in your home market on a real local phone and a warmed, niche-trained account.
principles.why: Alberto: about 1 in 10 videos goes viral on his Spain phone vs 1 in 30-35 on his VPN phone targeting the US; creators warm new accounts ~3 days by following niche micro accounts (not macro accounts).

principles.rule: Upload as a draft and publish from the phone with a native trending sound.
principles.why: TikTok's API cannot choose trending sounds; practitioners believe API-direct posts get less reach (unverified). Larry, Postiz's case study and Upload-Post all default to drafts.
principles.source: Oliver Henry (transcript); Postiz blog; Upload-Post pricing page

principles.rule: Keep every account's content original: no watermarks, no identical files across accounts.
principles.why: TikTok makes unoriginal or watermarked content For You-ineligible and treats identical content across accounts as spam; Instagram ranks originality up and down-ranks watermarked reposts and aggregators.
principles.source: ContentIQ TikTok rules (verified Sep 28 2026); Coruzant/Dataslayer on Instagram originality

principles.rule: Fix the in-app funnel: onboarding quiz and hard paywall matter as much as content.
principles.why: Larry's agent rewrote onboarding and produced the best new-user day in months; QUITTR credits its 12-screen quiz (99% completion) and hard paywall; RevenueCat 2026: hard paywall 10.7% vs freemium 2.1% download->paid (D35).
principles.source: Oliver Henry (transcript); Startup Spells on QUITTR; RevenueCat State of Subscription Apps 2026

principles.rule: Build product features that are content (trend-hooked features, widgets, shareable outputs).
principles.why: Jack watches viral content in his niche and builds features to hook into the trend; his top video hit 4M views and 503 comments mostly asking for the app name.

principles.rule: Once organic works, multiply it with paid creators on base + view-milestone bonuses, then run winners as ads.
principles.why: Typical deals: $10-30 base per video plus decreasing-CPM bonuses; viral.app median $16/video and $1 CPM; Cal AI targeted ~$5 CPM with ~150 influencers by month 7 and reused top organic videos as paid creative at ~$7K/day.
principles.source: Nicole (transcript); viral.app/ugc-rates (Oct 2026); Chris Koerner newsletter on Cal AI

principles.rule: Explore broadly first, then exploit: 5-6 formats in the first two weeks of a new account.
principles.why: Alberto treats >15K views on a new account as the signal a format can go viral; if nothing hits after exploration, rethink the app's positioning.

tiktok.posts_per_day: 1-3 per account (practitioners: Larry 3/day minimum, Alberto 3/day, Jack/Max ~2/day). Ramp new accounts: 1-2/day for 2 weeks, then up to 3.
tiktok.notes: Buffer (11.4M posts, 150K accounts): vs 1 post/week, 2-5/week = +17% views per post, 6-10 = +29%, 11+ = +34%; medians stay flat, so the gain is more lottery tickets. Studies conflict on exact times (Sprout favors Tue-Thu 14-18h), so switch to your own TikTok Studio data after ~30 posts. Post drafts and add a trending sound on the phone. Audited API clients have a reported cap of ~15 direct posts/creator/24h (3p, unverified).

reels.posts_per_day: 0.5-1 (3-5 per week minimum; 6-10+/week accelerates growth). Cross-post TikTok winners daily if available.
reels.notes: Buffer: follower growth rate +0.12%/week at 1-2 posts/week vs +0.26% at 3-5, +0.44% at 6-9, +0.66% at 10+; reach per post +12% at 3-5/week. Upload clean, watermark-free files. Use Trial Reels (shown to non-followers first) for hook tests [verify current behavior]. Shares/sends per reach are widely reported as the key signal for non-follower reach. API: 100 published posts per rolling 24h; API carousels max 10 items.

shorts.posts_per_day: 0.2-1 (Buffer baseline 1-3/week; practitioners repurpose TikTok winners daily).
shorts.notes: Track 'viewed vs swiped away': 70%+ viewed is strong, ~50/50 is average, under 30% dies (third-party bands; compare to your own median). View counting changed in March 2025, so compare only against recent Shorts. API: videos.insert default 100 calls/day.

x.posts_per_day: 3-5 (3-4 sustainable), including build-in-public updates and replies.
x.notes: Best for build-in-public: revenue screenshots, demo clips, changelog threads. X says links are no longer deboosted (Jul 28 2026), but third-party data still shows weak link posts; when in doubt put the link in a reply. Replying to comments adds ~8% engagement (Buffer). Avoid bursting many posts at once (reported, unverified). Hosted Postiz strips links from X posts.

linkedin.posts_per_day: 0.3-1 (2-5 per week; 11+/week roughly triples engagements per post vs once a week).
linkedin.notes: Carousels/document posts lead engagement; replying to comments adds ~30% engagement (Buffer). Best for B2B, dev tools and founder narrative; short native video works for launches.

benchmarks.hook_hold_rate: TikTok 3-second hold: 60-70% = good organic (grow-it), 70-80% typical for organic UGC (Agniverse, vendor); paid ads have a 33% median and 55% for the top 10% (Benly, 12K+ ads Q1 2026, via Agniverse). YouTube Shorts viewed-vs-swiped: 70%+ strong, ~50% average, under 30% dies.
benchmarks.completion: Sub-15s videos: 40-60% completion achievable; a healthy curve holds ~70% after 3s, ~60% at 15s, ~50% at 30s; 60s videos: 8-15% completion can still be healthy (third-party ranges, no official TikTok numbers). Slideshow vs video completion (68% vs 52%) is an unsourced claim.
benchmarks.views_to_installs: Organic blended 0.5-2% (5-20 installs per 1,000 views) per Agniverse (vendor, 5,800+ consumer-app videos); by format: slideshows 0.2-0.4%, silent/text 0.3-0.6%, reaction 0.4-0.8%, talking head 1-2%. Bio-link tap->install 1.1% (homepage), 1.4% (raw App Store URL), 3.6% (feature landing page), 5.2% (feature landing page + smart deep link) per tap-3 (vendor, 84 accounts, ~1.2M clicks). Download->paid median 2.0% globally; hard paywall 10.7% vs freemium 2.1% (RevenueCat 2026).
benchmarks.notes: Real anecdotes are far lower when the CTA is weak: 300K views -> ~0 downloads (Oliver Henry before fixing the CTA); 500K views -> ~40 installs (TokPortal example); ~2,000 views -> 11 downloads with a wrong-language listing (LifePilot). View distribution is extremely skewed: average ~11-12.5K views per video, 1-3% of videos exceed 100K, and 8 of 34 hooks produced 85%+ of views in one campaign (Agniverse). Many organic installs come via App Store search days later, so click-based attribution undercounts. Action thresholds per post: Larry skill 50K+ = make 3 variations, 10-50K = keep, 1-10K = one more variation, under 1K twice = drop; Agniverse: under 200 = account problem, 200-2K = weak hook, 2K-10K = weak retention, 10K+ = winner; Alberto: 15K+ on a new account = promising format.

iteration_loop: Research: collect 10-20 niche outliers (views divided by the creator's median, Sandcastles-style) and your own past winners; extract format, hook family, slide arc, audio mood.
Brief: regenerate the product brief from the codebase and the latest release (features, wow screens, pricing, persona, objections).
Generate: for each format, hold body/images/CTA constant and create 3-5 hook variants from different families (reveal, time-shock, forbidden, POV, listicle, mistakes).
Guardrail: check safe zones (no text in bottom 20% / top 10%), legibility, watermark-free, unique per account, AIGC label if realistic AI people, hashtags <= 5, CTA names the app.
Schedule: one variant per slot at consistent times (e.g., 07:30 / 16:30 / 21:00 local); keep the same CTA/link for 14+ days.
Publish: TikTok as draft -> phone notification -> add trending sound that matches the emotion -> post; Reels/Shorts/LinkedIn/X direct with clean files.

Measure at 24h and 72h: views, 3s hold, avg % watched/completion, shares, saves/sends, profile visits, link taps; join with installs (App Store Connect/Play Console sources, smart-link clicks, promo codes, HDYHAU survey) and trials/revenue (RevenueCat/Stripe).
Classify each post against thresholds (50K+ double down; 10-50K keep; 1-10K one more try; under 1K twice drop).

Diagnose with the 2x2: high views/low conversion -> fix CTA; low views/high conversion -> fix hook; both low -> new format; both high -> 3 variations plus more accounts; installs but no payers -> fix onboarding/paywall.
Exploit: clone winners into 3 variants, rotate between top hooks, track each hook's hit rate and retire it when it falls (e.g., under 1 hit in 5 posts).
Amplify: cross-post winners to Reels/Shorts, brief creators with the winning script, boost the best organic posts as Spark Ads/Meta ads.
Remember: write weekly learnings (winning hooks, dead hooks, CTA results, audio notes) to a per-app memory file the agent rereads before generating.
reach_killers: Another platform's watermark or logo in the video (TikTok FYF-ineligible; Instagram down-ranks watermarked reposts).
Reposting the same file or near-identical content across accounts (TikTok spam rule since Sep 2025); unoriginal content without creative edits (adding subtitles alone is insufficient).
AI-looking images and AI humans; landscape crops, black bars, wrong aspect ratio (Oliver Henry).
Text in the bottom 20% or top 10% of the frame (hidden by UI) or too small to read.
No sound, or music that doesn't match the emotion of the video.
Looking like an ad: hard pitch on slide 1, brand-first framing.
Brand-new cold accounts posting immediately, or accounts that post more than they consume (practitioner belief, unverified).
VPN/geo mismatch between phone, SIM and target market (Alberto: 1 in 30-35 viral vs 1 in 10 at home; mechanism unverified).
API-direct posting instead of draft + manual publish (practitioner consensus, unverified).
Hashtag stuffing (more than 5) and formulaic, long captions (Postiz case study).
Inconsistent, sporadic posting (Buffer: consistency compounds engagement per post).
Overusing one winning hook until it decays.
Undisclosed commercial content (TikTok, effective Sep 24 2026: may reduce visibility or force the disclosure toggle).
Unlabeled realistic AI content (may be removed, restricted or labeled by TikTok).
On X: link-only posts still underperform per third-party data despite the official 'no penalty' line; bursts of many posts reportedly reduce reach (unverified).
Conversion killers (not reach): CTA that never names the app, raw App Store links opened in in-app browsers, switching bio links weekly, wrong-language store listing.
traffic_routing: Name the app and the outcome on the CTA slide and in the caption; offer 'search [App] on the App Store' because many organic installs come via store search days later.

TikTok bio: a clickable link needs 1,000 followers (personal) or a verified business account; personal accounts cannot link directly to App Store pages (blocked since 2023), business accounts can and get a 'Download app' button.

Send bio traffic to a feature-specific landing page that matches the video, not the homepage or raw store URL (tap-3, vendor: 1.1% homepage, 1.4% raw App Store, 3.6% feature page, 5.2% feature page + smart deep link).
Escape the in-app browser (redirect to the default browser or use smart links) before showing the store: 3.8x installs in tap-3's data (vendor).
Swap the landing page daily to match the top-performing video (2.1x installs vs one generic page; tap-3, vendor), but keep one link/CTA for 14+ days.
Write benefit-led CTA copy that omits 'app'/'download' (e.g., 'Record your first workout free'): +27% install rate (tap-3, vendor).
Use deferred deep links (Branch, AppsFlyer, Adjust) so installs land on the promised feature and skip generic onboarding: 2.4x D7 retention (tap-3, vendor).

Attribute organic traffic: App Store campaign links (pt/ct tokens) and Play Store UTM referrers per account or post; unique promo codes per account/creator; an in-app 'How did you hear about us?' onboarding step; App Store Connect and Play Console source reports.
Connect RevenueCat or Stripe so every post/hook/CTA gets revenue, not just views (Larry loop, LarryLoop, Volume).
Reply to 'what's the app?' comments with the name and pin it; comment volume is itself a reach signal (Jack: 503 comments on a 4M-view video, mostly asking the app name).
Instagram: use the bio link (up to 5), story link stickers and comment-to-DM automations; Reels caption links are not clickable.
X/LinkedIn: link in the post is officially fine on X since Jul 2026, but test link-in-reply vs link-in-post; use UTM-tagged links per post.

feature_ideas.name: Codebase -> Product Brief
feature_ideas.why: No competitor understands the product; Claude Code/Codex can read README, screens, routes, paywall/pricing config, onboarding copy, App Store metadata and recent commits to produce features ranked by visual wow, persona, pains, proof and objections that every template uses.

feature_ideas.name: Real-app footage capture (iOS Simulator, Android emulator, Playwright)
feature_ideas.why: Hook+demo videos and 'dramatic screenshot' CTA slides need real screens; xcrun simctl recordVideo / adb screenrecord / Playwright let the agent script flows and capture them automatically; developers already have these tools.

feature_ideas.name: Slideshow engine with platform-safe text rendering
feature_ideas.why: Most of the proven app growth (Larry, Alberto, UMAX) is slideshows; bake in the proven spec: 9:16 (1080x1920 / 1024x1536), 3-6 slide arcs, ~28% vertical text placement, 4-6 words per line, stroke outline, TikTok-native-style fonts, safe zones, consistent scene across slides.

feature_ideas.name: Hook Lab: variants, controlled tests and a hook ledger
feature_ideas.why: Hooks drive reach; generate 3-5 variants per body across hook families, rotate them across slots, track hit rate and decay per hook, auto-make 3 variations of anything over 50K and retire hooks that stop hitting.

feature_ideas.name: Draft-first publishing with phone handoff, plus direct posting where safe
feature_ideas.why: TikTok's API can't pick trending sounds and unaudited clients post private-only; push TikTok drafts with a phone notification (add sound, post in ~60s), post directly to IG/YT/LinkedIn/X via official APIs, or plug in Post Bridge/Upload-Post/self-hosted Postiz as the posting backend.

feature_ideas.name: Revenue loop and 2x2 diagnosis
feature_ideas.why: Connect RevenueCat, Stripe, App Store Connect and Play Console; attribute installs and revenue per post via smart links, promo codes and survey answers; show the views x conversion 2x2 with explicit thresholds and recommended next action.

feature_ideas.name: Pre-post guardrails
feature_ideas.why: Prevent reach killers: watermark detection (TikTok, CapCut, Sora/other generators), per-account uniqueness (no identical files), safe-zone and legibility checks, AIGC label prompt for realistic AI people, commercial disclosure toggle, hashtag cap of 5, caption length, CTA-names-the-app check.

feature_ideas.name: BYO AI with per-post cost meter and flat pricing
feature_ideas.why: Credits, expiring balances and cancellation friction are the category's most common complaints (Arcads 2.6 on Trustpilot, OpusClip, MakeUGC); using the user's own Claude Code/Codex plus image API keys makes honest flat pricing possible.

feature_ideas.name: Hook + demo video template and basic editor (captions, trims, overlays)
feature_ideas.why: Hook+demo is the second core app format (Oliver generated ~400 combos per batch before Larry; Fastlane sells it); needs animated captions (Submagic-style presets), text hooks, trims and audio placeholders.

feature_ideas.name: Attribution plumbing as pull requests
feature_ideas.why: Shipreel has repo access: open PRs that add a 'How did you hear about us?' onboarding step, deep-link and UTM capture, App Store campaign tokens and Play referrers, RevenueCat attributes and per-creator promo codes. No marketing tool can do this.

feature_ideas.name: Feature landing pages with in-app-browser escape and smart store redirect
feature_ideas.why: Vendor data: feature page + smart deep link 5.2% vs raw App Store 1.4%, browser escape 3.8x, daily page matching the top video 2.1x; generate pages in the user's web repo and deploy to their Vercel/Netlify.

feature_ideas.name: Format cloning from reference videos and an outlier scanner
feature_ideas.why: Practitioners copy proven formats; let users paste reference URLs (analyzed via frames + transcript) and maintain a watchlist of niche accounts with outlier scores (views divided by the creator's median), Sandcastles-style but with no credit burn.

feature_ideas.name: Analytics ingestion via screenshot OCR and CSV exports; Trial Reels workflow
feature_ideas.why: Retention metrics (3s hold, completion) aren't fully available via APIs for most accounts; Oliver sent screenshots to Larry; Claude vision can parse TikTok Studio retention screens; Trial Reels give clean hook tests on Instagram.

feature_ideas.name: Post-install coach
feature_ideas.why: When installs are good but payers aren't, propose onboarding quiz and paywall changes as code with RevenueCat benchmarks (hard paywall 10.7% vs freemium 2.1%); Larry's onboarding rewrite produced the best day of new users.

feature_ideas.name: Multi-account and multi-market manager with warm-up checklist and localization
feature_ideas.why: Growth scales via accounts per niche/market (Alberto: 6-7 accounts per phone, Spain first, separate English phone); provide human warm-up checklists/timers, per-account voice and uniqueness, localized variants; never automate fake engagement.

feature_ideas.name: Changelog -> build-in-public posts and 'what's new' shorts
feature_ideas.why: Developer-native channels (X, LinkedIn) are missing from slideshow tools; git commits and releases are a free content stream with real proof.

feature_ideas.name: Templates as code plus timeline editor
feature_ideas.why: Version-controlled, forkable templates the agent can edit (React/Remotion-style); if embedding Remotion, budget for the Automators license ($0.01/render, $100/mo minimum).

feature_ideas.name: Agent chat surface and per-app memory files
feature_ideas.why: Larry is steered by WhatsApp messages and recovers from context loss via memory files; offer chat (desktop, phone push/Telegram/Slack) and a durable winners/losers ledger per app.

feature_ideas.name: Shipreel MCP server and CLI
feature_ideas.why: Agent surfaces are table stakes (Postiz, Post Bridge, Blotato, Genviral, Volume, Upload-Post); developers will script Shipreel from Claude Code/Codex.

feature_ideas.name: Creator mode: briefs, course, content bank, payouts
feature_ideas.why: Once a format works, creators multiply it; auto-generate scripts with per-line emotion and shot lists, onboarding course outline, content bank, payout calculator (base + milestone bonuses, e.g., $16 median/video, $1 CPM) and creator account tracking (viral.app-style).

feature_ideas.name: AI UGC avatars with realism gate and disclosure
feature_ideas.why: Talking heads convert best per view (1-2% vs 0.2-0.4% for slideshows), but AI actors draw 'clearly AI' complaints; offer only with a realism review step and automatic AIGC labeling.

feature_ideas.name: Paid amplification export
feature_ideas.why: Cal AI and QUITTR scaled by running top organic creatives as ads; export winners with naming conventions and Spark Ads code workflows; suggest budgets ($50-100/day start, +25%/week at 1.2-2x ROAS per Rork).

feature_ideas.name: Virality score as triage only
feature_ideas.why: OpusClip users find a virality score useful for prioritizing; train it on the user's own history and show it as a ranking aid, not a promise.

feature_ideas.name: Studio mode (many apps, approvals, team seats)
feature_ideas.why: App studios run many apps and accounts; per-app workspaces, approval queues and shared hook libraries.

feature_ideas.name: Optional Android 'add sound and publish' helper
feature_ideas.why: The Postiz case study used a ~$50 Android phone over ADB to pick trending audio and publish drafts; useful for power users but carries platform-automation risk, so keep it opt-in and clearly labeled.

competitors.name: ReelFarm
competitors.pricing: Growth $49/mo (100 slideshows, 10 formats); Scale $95 (250, 20 formats); Enterprise $195 (750, 200 formats, BYO Anthropic key). 3 free TikToks. (site, Oct 2026)
competitors.strengths: Original TikTok slideshow automation; format library from real businesses; set-and-forget automations; unlimited accounts and seats; API + Skill.md; strong brand among faceless-page operators.
competitors.weaknesses: TikTok-only native posting (Reels/Shorts export only); tracks views, not installs or revenue; Pinterest-sourced images raise rights questions; limits count generated slideshows; thin independent reviews (Product Hunt 3.0/5 from 2, one alleging 0% sales and 30% churn).

competitors.name: LarryLoop (Oliver Henry)
competitors.pricing: Starter $39/mo (1 post/day, 1 project); Growth $99 (3/day, 3 projects); Scale $249 (10/day, unlimited). (site)
competitors.strengths: Productized Larry loop with per-post revenue attribution (Stripe, RevenueCat) and an iteration engine that kills losing hooks; credible founder story; '11,000+ users' (self-reported).
competitors.weaknesses: TikTok-only; generic product understanding from web research; posting method (draft vs direct) unclear; the free Larry skill undercuts it.

competitors.name: Larry skill (OpenClaw / LarryBrain)
competitors.pricing: Free skill; pay for OpenClaw host, model (e.g., Claude Max) and image API.
competitors.strengths: Most specific public playbook (slide spec, overlay rules, times, warm-up, thresholds, 2x2 diagnosis); TikTok drafts via Postiz; RevenueCat loop; widely copied (Upload-Post fork).
competitors.weaknesses: DIY setup (Docker/VPS), context drift, fragile auth, operator-dependent; one channel and one format; no UI or editor.

competitors.name: Volume
competitors.pricing: Core $29.99/mo (60 posts, 100 AI images); Pro $69.99 (300 posts, 400 images); 3-day trial; only posted slideshows count. (site blog, Sep 2026)
competitors.strengths: App-focused; 'App shots' (screenshot to realistic phone-in-hand photo); trend research to approvals; RevenueCat analytics; MCP + API + Skill.md; managed enterprise tier.
competitors.weaknesses: TikTok-only for now (Instagram 'coming soon'); direct auto-posting (no sound step); little independent review coverage.

competitors.name: Fastlane
competitors.pricing: Free plan; paid from $29/mo; human-warmed TikTok/IG accounts $100/account/mo.
competitors.strengths: URL-to-content (slideshows, AI UGC with 1,000+ characters, hook+demo, memes from 25K+ trending videos); native posting to TikTok, Reels, Shorts, LinkedIn; per-post signup/sales attribution.
competitors.weaknesses: Learns from your website, not your product; selling warmed accounts carries platform ToS risk; most comparison content is self-published.

competitors.name: Genviral
competitors.pricing: Creator $29/mo; Professional $49; Business $99; Scale $199; ~17% off annual (site). Hosted accounts reportedly $450 for 5 (unverified).
competitors.strengths: Scheduler + AI Studio (30+ models, 200+ templates incl. slideshows) on 10 networks; competitor tracking; 'Vira' autopilot; CLI with 60+ commands and an open-source agent skill for OpenClaw/Claude Code/Codex.
competitors.weaknesses: Shared credits across features; confusing free/paid messaging; hosted accounts on dedicated devices are a ToS gray area.

competitors.name: Blotato
competitors.pricing: Starter $29/mo (1,250 credits, 20 accounts); Creator $97 (5,000 credits, 40 accounts); Agency $499 (28,000 credits). 7-day trial without API. (site)
competitors.strengths: AI writing/images/faceless video/voice + remix + publishing to 9 platforms; API + MCP; n8n/Make nodes; Trustpilot 4.8 (388 reviews).
competitors.weaknesses: Credits run out (one estimate ~24 faceless videos/mo on Starter); learning curve and glitches; creator-brand-centric; light analytics; no revenue loop.

competitors.name: Postiz
competitors.pricing: Hosted: Standard $29/mo (5 channels), Team $39 (10), Pro $49 (30), Ultimate $99 (100); ~20% off annual. Open source (AGPL-3.0) self-host free plus infra (~$5-10/mo).
competitors.strengths: 30 platforms; MCP, CLI and API on every plan; webhooks, n8n/Make/Zapier; used by Larry for TikTok drafts; self-hostable.
competitors.weaknesses: Hosted version strips all URLs from X posts (issue #1939 closed 'not planned' Sep 30 2026); self-hosting requires your own platform app approvals; no creative judgment or revenue loop.

competitors.name: Post Bridge
competitors.pricing: Free (5 posts/mo); Marketer $39/mo (15 accounts, API, MCP); Operator $99 (99 accounts, then $1/account). 7-day trial. (site, Oct 2026)
competitors.strengths: Simple flat pricing; 10 platforms incl. TikTok carousels; API and MCP included; ChatGPT app (Sep 2026); 1,400+ paying customers (self-reported).
competitors.weaknesses: Pure distribution: no creative, no analytics loop; older listings show different tiers, so pricing has churned.

competitors.name: Upload-Post
competitors.pricing: Not shown on pricing page; free trial; positioned cheaper than Ayrshare ($49+) (unverified).
competitors.strengths: 22 platforms; REST API + SDKs; MCP server with 40 tools (MIT, hosted or npx); white-label API; recommends TikTok draft mode; powers a Larry skill fork.
competitors.weaknesses: Infrastructure only; carousel support not confirmed on the page.

competitors.name: Buffer
competitors.pricing: Free (3 channels); Essentials ~$5-6/channel/mo; Team ~$10-12/channel/mo (3p).
competitors.strengths: Simplest scheduler; strong free tier; publishes large-sample posting research.
competitors.weaknesses: No creative generation, no app attribution, no iteration loop.

competitors.name: Later
competitors.pricing: ~$18.75-25 / $37.50-50 / $82.50-110 per month; no free tier; 14-day trial (3p, sources conflict).
